analysis: The trial succeeded with host validation macro HR@10 of 0.5200, versus the reported prior 0.5188 (+0.0012). Electronics rose from 0.36 to 0.40. Current category HR@10 values were Movies_and_TV 0.535, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.530, Electronics 0.400, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.615. The small macro gain supports retaining training-history exclusion for further comparison, but does not establish a reliable improvement or causality. The change masks shared sampled negatives found anywhere in a user's complete training history, including outside the sampled window, while preserving positive-collision masking, 192 uniform draws with duplicates, and equal user weighting. No test metrics were available. Allocated GPU time was 478.50 seconds.
code_summary: One independently trained taste-aware SASRec per category, with exactly one selected checkpoint loaded for prediction. Each network uses 96-dimensional item and position embeddings, two causal attention blocks with two heads, dropout 0.25, and a gated cumulative causal taste representation. Scores use normalized item/sequence vectors, a learned clamped scale, and jointly trained item biases. Sorted unique train-only histories are padded by a deterministic collator; batched searchsorted identifies sampled negatives to mask at each supervised position. Training retains AdamW, seed 42, random-window sampling, a default 200-epoch limit, validation every five epochs plus the first/final epochs, and early stopping after 40 epochs without improvement. Inference architecture, predictor writer, dataset routing, and trial-local artifact paths are preserved.
